raw_response:
I will put 10 mu into my usual wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest part of my farm and I have well irrigation to support it. On the remaining 6.1 mu, I will split the land into cotton, millet, mung bean, and peanut so I do not depend on only one crop and so the work is still manageable for my age and my two-person household. I will keep inputs moderate, not extreme. I will use better seed where it clearly helps yield and stability, but I will not push fertilizer or water too hard because I want reliable harvests, controlled costs, and work I can finish on time. For wheat and maize, I will feed them more because they are my main grain crops. For millet and mung bean, I will keep inputs lighter because they tolerate leaner management. Cotton needs more plant protection, so I will plan for that. Peanut needs balanced fertilizer, especially phosphorus and potassium, so I will not treat it like maize.
